subject.title: [Feature]: Add local owner/appliance mode for fully trusted non-admin OpenClaw deployments

question: Should a configured local service identity retain a pre-approved broad operator scope baseline across repairs and reconnects without interactive scope-upgrade approval, and what proof must bind it to the dedicated OS account?
rationale: Current main deliberately prevents silent scope widening, while the requested unattended model needs durable authority; acceptable identity proof, maximum scopes, and recovery semantics are security policy choices.

options.title: Bounded Verified Identity
options.body: Add explicit enrollment backed by OS-account or host-key proof, fixed maximum scopes, audit output, revocation, and a readiness diagnostic.

options.title: Diagnostics Only
options.body: Keep scope upgrades interactive, document the existing no-prompt execution profile, and add preflight checks for token and pairing drift.

options.title: Broad Owner Mode
options.body: Add one aggregate switch that suppresses local execution and scope approvals inside the account boundary, accepting a substantially larger trust contract.

recommendation.title: Bounded Verified Identity
recommendation.body: Add explicit enrollment backed by OS-account or host-key proof, fixed maximum scopes, audit output, revocation, and a readiness diagnostic.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history places pairing, verified auto-approval, and gateway authorization design with this feature owner and merger.
